extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary criticism: critics, students of literature, poets, editors, and informed general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Critical criteria for judging poetic works and editions and for assessing histories of the theatre: includes qualities of editorial arrangement and illustration, poetic technique (imagery, sound, sincerity), and the value of anecdote and social context in theatrical history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid, vivacious historical narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: A history of the drama should be singularly varied and vivacious, full of the colours of life, concentrating and artificially intensifying the character and conditions of ordinary life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat stage history as an agreeable addition to personal memoirs; gather anecdotes and scattered picturesque details so the narrative serves as a lively mirror of social life and manners rather than a dry chronology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations that enhance understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: An illustrated edition should add substantial charm through abundant, first-rate illustrations appropriate to subject and execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include several complementary kinds of illustration (e.g., copper-plate likenesses of actors, detailed woodcuts of theatrical topography, and lively tail-pieces). Vignettes should capture atmosphere—minute detail with a theatrical 'light'—and materially enhance the reader's sense of place and history (examples: Bear-garden and Swan Theatre vignettes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Portraits revealing actors' character
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits of actors and theatrical personages should help explain the power and range of the players they portray.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer portraits that convey expressive physiognomy—'speaking eyes', blent strength and delicacy, or other features that suggest an actor's stage presence and range. Be aware many portraits do not fully account for performative power; comparative or series images (e.g., tail-pieces of Garrick) can illustrate variety better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of anecdotes and impromptus to humanize history
rubrics_metrics.description: A theatrical history gains charm and humanity from abundant anecdotes, impromptus, and witticisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and deploy illustrative stories (e.g., Foote's quips, Jevon's stage gambits, curious episodes) to reveal character, cheerfulness, and the social texture of stage life rather than relying solely on abstract commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to social context and staging customs
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of theatrical life should record contemporary customs and audience behaviour (admission practices, encores, mingling of public and players) to illuminate how performance was experienced and produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how audience habits (drinking, brawling, encore customs) and institutional rules affected performance and reception—these details explain historical differences in acting and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial arrangement chosen to illuminate
rubrics_metrics.description: The arrangement of a collected edition should be chosen for its pedagogical or critical utility—e.g., printing poems with dates in order of composition has indisputable recommendations for students, while grouping by subject reveals poetic motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether chronology (shows development) or subject-grouping (shows thematic coherence) better serves readers' aims; justify editorial choices to aid study of the poet's genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate poet's temperament and life to poetic character
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical assessment should consider the influence of the poet's personal temperament and material circumstances (e.g., Wordsworth's calm contentment) on the physiognomy of their poetic creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for connections between biographical temperament (cheerful, placid, ascetic, tragic) and recurring tonal qualities, themes, or modes of perception in the poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish fancy from imagination (intensity levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism should discriminate between lower and higher degrees of imaginative intensity—'fancy' versus 'imagination'—and assess where individual poems sit on that scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree of concentration and collectedness of the poet's conception; identify passages that evidence 'higher' imaginative power versus more superficial or derivative fancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for disciplined, attentive reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain poetry requires and rewards a disciplined 'reading between the lines'—a cultivated temper and intellectual concentration to apprehend depth beneath surface phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag works that are initiatory: those that bestow special illumination only if the reader follows a 'difficult way' of sustained attention and temperamental discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid, precise sensory imagery (visual and aural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Great poetry shows clear, delicate outlining of visible imagery and scrupulous noting of sounds; it realizes abstract impressions (silence, darkness, motionlessness) as sensuous experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value fine particulars (e.g., harebell, single sheep, rustling corn, subtle sound-effects). Assess how imagery and sound together shape the poem's mood and intellectual effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endowing nature with moral or spiritual life
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry may present natural objects as possessing moral or spiritual life—making landscape a companion to human moods and a vehicle for thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how effectively the poet elevates nature to a quasi-human presence that dignifies or subdues humanity, and how that relationship informs theme and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of humble, common subjects for sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing incidents and language from humble life is a deliberate aesthetic: such subjects are nearer to nature and offer more direct, impassioned expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'language really used by men' in select vivid moments, not the dead level of ordinary speech; judge whether simple subject-matter yields authentic, ennobled feeling rather than tame calmness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical mastery, finish, and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: A poet's command of technique—equality of finish across varied forms, perfect balance between matter and form, delicate cadences and transitions, logic of poetic structure—is a central criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for uniform high craft ('even finish'), mastery of diverse forms, structural coherence (the 'intaglio' faculty), and the graceful handling of cadences and transitions; these mark a 'poetic scholar' of high accomplishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive power in still-life and landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: An aptitude for vivid description—still-life, landscape, and novel motives (e.g., northern summer scenes)—is a measurable poetic gift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the freshness and exactness of descriptive passages and how they contribute to overall emotional and imaginative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality balanced with scholarly restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality is valued but often tempered by scholarship; a poet may be highly accomplished in craft yet modest in overt originality—too much learnedness can produce 'spasmodic' lapses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize genuine originality but beware forced novelty; recognize when learned technique enhances rather than stifles imaginative individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for sustained power across long pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer poems should maintain sustained poetic power and technical command over their length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether extended works (examples cited: 'The New Endymion') keep their energy, coherence, and inventive force throughout, rather than flagging or breaking into unevenness.
